text:
Korean President Lee Jae Myung was set to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday to discuss ways to enhance bilateral cooperation.
The meeting comes as Lee arrived in Shenzhen, China, earlier in the day to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which runs through Thursday.
The upcoming talks mark the two leaders' third bilateral summit, following their first meeting in November in Gyeongju, the Korean city that hosted the 2025 APEC summit. They last met in Beijing in January when Lee visited China.
During Wednesday's meeting, Lee and Xi are expected to assess progress in bilateral relations and discuss ways to expand trade and investment, as well as people-to-people and cultural exchanges, Lee's spokesperson Kim Sung-wan said in a press release.
Lee and Xi also plan to discuss issues of mutual interest, including cooperation to promote peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula, Kim noted.
The talks are expected to provide an opportunity to set the course of further development of the two countries' strategic partnership ahead of the 35th anniversary next year of the establishment of diplomatic relations, the spokesperson said.
